title: Beyond the 956: Teen arrested, charged with murder in fatal shooting of 15-year-old walking to school in the Bronx
excerpt: A 17-year-old was arrested Wednesday and charged with murder, manslaughter and criminal possession of a weapon in the Oct. 29 fatal shooting of a 15-year-old boy walking to school in the Bronx. The suspect has not been publicly identified because he is a minor, and investigators are still searching for additional suspects.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A 17-year-old was arrested Wednesday, November 11, 2026, and charged with murder in the fatal shooting of a 15-year-old boy who was walking to school in the Bronx on October 29, New York police said.

The teenager, who has not been publicly identified because he is a minor, was also charged with manslaughter and criminal possession of a weapon, according to the New York Police Department. He was taken into custody at his home in the Bronx on Wednesday morning and brought to the 42nd Precinct for questioning.

The 15-year-old, a student at DreamYard Preparatory School who had immigrated from Ghana about a year earlier, was shot in the stomach shortly before 9:30 a.m. on Thursday, October 29, near East 171st Street and Crotona Place in the Claremont neighborhood of the Bronx, police said. He was taken to St. Barnabas Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

Surveillance footage showed the boy running as someone chased him before he was shot, according to reports. Investigators said three teenagers fled the scene, and police are still searching for as many as two more suspects.

The boy's father has said his son had been bullied at school, and two students were reportedly suspended after an incident. Authorities have not confirmed whether the reported bullying was connected to the shooting, and police have not announced a motive. Investigators said they are looking at bullying and robbery as potential motives.

The boy's family spoke at a news conference Wednesday at the National Action Network's House of Justice in Harlem, joined by Rev. Al Sharpton and civil rights attorney Ben Crump, calling for accountability and answers about how the boy got a gun and how his school handled the reported bullying.

The charges are allegations. The 17-year-old is presumed innocent until proven guilty in court.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) Instagram post, Nov. 11, 2026; New York Post; PEOPLE; ABC News.
